newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mixed on Tuesday with the longer end solidly higher, boosted by a strong showing in Bunds after the German central bank held its repo rate at an unchanged fixed rate of three percent, dealers said.
But the market continued to reckon on near-term changes in German interest rates, they said, keeping the short end weak and setting the guilder yield curve back in flattening mode.
Dutch bonds lagged the German market in the afternoon, putting spreads under pressure. One trader said the yield discount to Bunds was starting to make a long-predicted move back to parity.

The market is now seen focusing on the slew of U.S. data due later in the week to set the tone for trading. July retail sales and producer prices figures are due on Wednesday, followed by July consumer prices on Thursday.
A broker said the retail sales data was likely to come in strong and could spook the U.S. market and feed through into Europe, so players were staying cautious.
However, the local market could stay supported by positive sentiment in Bund futures, with the September contract well up through key levels on Tuesday, he added.
